description: Stage 3, Gate 3a: a structured trace of every turn, and open threads as first-class objects. This is the data layer everything else (predictor, sleep replay, self-build) needs to exist before it can be trusted, and it directly targets the tangent-handling failure: every unfinished thought in a message becomes a tracked object instead of being dropped.

userStories.title: Every turn writes a structured trace record
userStories.description: On every real conversation turn (the production CognitiveTurnResult path, not a test harness), write one JSON record: raw input, memories retrieved, any predictions made, the assembled prompt sections, the model output, and per-stage latency (embed/retrieve/prompt-build/generate/post-process). This is pure logging — no new behavior, no model changes.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: a trace record is written for every turn that goes through the real production entry point, not a mock/test-only path
AC2: record includes input text, retrieved memory IDs, prompt section boundaries, output text, and stage timings in milliseconds
AC3: traces are stored locally, append-only, with a replay_turn(id) function that can re-run a past turn's stored input against current logic
AC4: no PII leaves the device — this is a local file/DB, not a network call
AC5: negative control: if trace writing is disabled, a test asserts the trace file does not grow — proves the wiring is real, not a stub
userStories.notes: AC1: every real turn through the production entry writes exactly one record — proven through the REAL JVM-executable composition root TermuxJarvisServer(port=0, backendOverride=FakeModelBackend(), turnTraceStore=JsonlTurnTraceStore(tempfile)) driven through the REAL LatencyPipeline.onUserInput -> CognitiveEngine.process(sendBlock=bridgeSend) call path (the /api/chat production chain); the ONLY swapped hop is the last one (recording collector instead of modelManager.send) — the store itself is a real file. 2 pipeline turns -> exactly 2 records, each carrying the exact raw input (TurnTraceProductionWiringTest). AC2: store-level round trip proves every field survives JSON (inputText, retrievedMemoryIds, promptSections offsets+length, outputText, crossSessionMemories, stageTimingsMs) plus all 5 canonical stage keys embed/retrieve/prompt-build/generate/post-process in ms; the live record's user-input prompt section starts at offset 0 with length==inputText.length and the generationPayload equals the payload captured at the bridge; the model output text is captured when generation answers synchronously (modelCall seam -> outputText=='Noted: green.'). AC3: replay_turn(id) re-runs the byte-identical stored input against the CURRENT engine (runner invoked), storedInput(id) reads it back, unknown id -> null without invoking the runner. AC4: append-only local file (JSON Lines; JarvisEngine.init writes under filesDir/traces, JVM harness under java.io.tmpdir), JsonlTurnTraceStore is a pure java.io.File store with no network — verifyCommand greps the whole trace package for zero HttpURLConnection/OkHttp/Retrofit/java.net.Socket references and the test asserts serialized records carry no http/socket markers. AC5 negative control THROUGH the real path: store disabled -> a full pipeline turn adds zero bytes and zero records (file length provably unchanged); re-enabled -> per-turn growth resumes — the wiring is real, not a stub. Wiring: CognitiveEngine got a nullable turnTraceStore seam (default null keeps the pre-trace path byte-for-byte), filled by JarvisEngine.init + TermuxJarvisServer; SystemGraph registers trace.turnTraceStore as a REAL TRACE organ (not PLANNED) with a cognitive.engine -> trace.turnTraceStore SENDS_TO edge reachable from entry.latencyPipeline (pinned by SystemGraphTest).

userStories.title: Unfinished/tangent thoughts become tracked thread objects, not discarded text
userStories.description: When a user message contains more than one distinct thought (a task plus an aside, an unfinished sentence, a jump to an unrelated topic), each becomes a Thread object: id, content, completeness (finished/trailing-off), a decay clock, and a link back to the turn it came from. The main task gets a main_anchor pointer that survives any number of tangents. This must work in mixed English/Egyptian Arabic/Franco-Arabic input — test fixtures include all three from this story onward.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: segment_message() splits one message into its separate thoughts; each becomes a Thread with its own completeness score
AC2: the reply acknowledges every open thread in one clause each without abandoning the main topic (thread_acknowledge) — it does not turn every message into a checklist
AC3: an unfinished thought is stored as incomplete, never auto-completed or invented
AC4: resurface_policy() brings a thread back on an idle moment or related topic, gated by its decay clock, not on a fixed timer alone
AC5: close_detect() notices when the user resolves a thread themselves without being told to

AC6: acceptance test three_thoughts_test(): one message with three unrelated thoughts, one half-finished — all three get answered, the open one is marked, and it correctly resurfaces in a later turn. Fixtures include at least one Egyptian Arabic and one Franco-Arabic case
AC7: negative control: with THREAD-OBJECTS disabled, three_thoughts_test() must fail (proves the test isn't vacuously passing)

userStories.title: Separate relevance, importance, uncertainty, novelty, consent, and cost from raw prediction error
userStories.description: Do not let a single prediction-error scalar drive encoding strength. A repeated, explicitly-stated boundary is unsurprising by definition but must never lose weight. Compute distinct signals and keep them distinct in storage; only combine them into one score later, and only after testing the combination against a simpler baseline (most-recent-N or keyword-match) shows it's actually better.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: importance is scored separately from novelty — an explicitly repeated instruction scores high importance regardless of how many times it's been said
AC2: each of the six signals (relevance, importance, uncertainty, novelty, consent, cost) is stored as its own field on the memory/thread record, not pre-collapsed
AC3: a fixture proves the bug this fixes: a boundary stated 5 times in test data must retain its top-tier importance score on the 5th mention, not decay
AC4: no combined single score is computed or used by any consumer yet — that's a later story, gated on baseline comparison
AC5: negative control: reverting to a naive single prediction-error scalar makes AC3's fixture fail
